Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that structural characteristics of a general practice can influence its adoption of new IT innovations in primary care. A study found that post-graduate education in the relevant clinical condition may play a critical role in spreading uptake beyond initial GP enthusiasts.

In other words, if your general practice is well-equipped to provide advanced clinical services and has staff members with specialized training, it is more likely to adopt new technologies that can support these efforts. Conversely, if your practice lacks such capabilities or resources, you may be less likely to adopt IT innovations.

This suggests that factors such as the availability of specialists, the quality of care provided, and the willingness to invest in new technologies are all important considerations when determining whether a general practice will adopt an IT innovation.
